sections.body: Many routes lead to good careers: university, vocational college, apprenticeships, starting a business, or working and studying later. None is the only 'right' path.
Explore: what do you enjoy, what are you good at, what does the world need, and what pays enough? Talk to people doing jobs you're curious about.
Set SMART goals: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound. 'Learn basic Python by finishing a free course by June' beats 'get better at coding'.
Reflect regularly: what's working, what isn't, what will I change?

options: Finish a free online Spanish course and hold a 5-minute conversation by December
hints: SMART goals are specific and have a deadline.
Can you measure whether it's achieved?
'Run 5 km without stopping by March' is SMART. 'Get fitter' isn't.
quiz.explain: It's specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound.

quiz.q: Which statement about career paths is most accurate?
options: There are many routes, including apprenticeships and vocational training
Only university leads to a good career
Your first job decides your whole career
hints: Think about all the routes in the lesson.
Many skilled careers start with apprenticeships.
Electricians, chefs and pilots often train through routes other than a traditional degree.
quiz.explain: There are many valid routes to a good career.
